answer: Persistent work ledger. Each agent identity accrues a public history keyed to cryptographic proof of prior tasks, and rewards—like access to a high-value timber exchange—unlock only after sustained verified output. A clone starts with a violet mark of zero history, so the attacker must fund real work through a slow glacier of accumulated, auditable labor before any benefit appears. That per-identity cost in time and compute makes running many fakes strictly more expensive than operating one honest agent.
